preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost reflects typical test burden: Small = existing record / standard labs  |  Medium = targeted test ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = biopsy or complement genetics ($1,500–$8,000+)  |  ⚠ Positive ANA/ANCA SUBTRACT points — recalculate if autoimmune markers are positive.

questions.question: Is there a progressive CKD trajectory with declining eGFR over months to years (decline >3 mL/min/1.73m²/year confirmed on serial values)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — progressive CKD documented on serial eGFR measurements

questions.question: Is persistent microscopic or gross hematuria present on ≥2 separate urinalysis reports?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — persistent hematuria confirmed; nearly universal in C3G

questions.question: Is proteinuria >0.5 g/day or ACR >30 mg/g present on urine protein quantification?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — proteinuria confirmed; variable degree from mild to nephrotic

questions.question: Is serum C3 persistently low (below normal on ≥2 separate measurements)? — HALLMARK finding of C3G from alternative pathway activation
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — persistently low C3 confirmed; primary laboratory hallmark of C3G

questions.question: Is serum C4 normal with C3 low? (Low C3 + normal C4 = alternative pathway activation; both low = classical pathway/SLE)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — C4 normal confirming alternative pathway pattern; distinguishes C3G from SLE

questions.question: Is C3 nephritic factor (C3NeF) positive on specialized complement testing?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — C3NeF positive; stabilizes C3 convertase, driving chronic C3 consumption

questions.question: Is soluble C5b-9 (sC5b-9/terminal complement complex) elevated above reference range?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — elevated sC5b-9 confirming ongoing terminal complement pathway activation

questions.question: Are ANA and anti-dsDNA both negative? (Positive ANA ≥1:80 or anti-dsDNA = subtract 10 pts — redirects to SLE nephritis)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — lupus nephritis excluded; ANA and anti-dsDNA negative (+3 pts)

questions.question: Is ANCA (MPO/PR3) negative? (Positive ANCA = subtract 10 pts — redirects to ANCA-associated vasculitis)
Are SPEP/UPEP and serum free light chains normal with no M-spike? (Abnormal paraprotein = subtract 5 pts — redirects to monoclonal GN)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — monoclonal gammopathy excluded; paraprotein screen negative (+2 pts)

questions.question: Is there C3-dominant staining (≥2+ brighter than IgG, IgA, IgM, C1q, and C4d) in an MPGN or mesangial pattern on immunofluorescence? — DEFINITIVE for C3G
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — C3-dominant IF pattern confirmed; DEFINITIVE diagnosis of C3G

questions.question: Does electron microscopy confirm subtype: intramembranous GBM deposits (Dense Deposit Disease/DDD) vs. mesangial/subendothelial deposits (C3GN)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — EM subtype confirmed; DDD = worse prognosis and higher transplant recurrence risk

high.label: 🔴  ≥80 High confidence C3G (biopsy-proven + low C3 + clinical syndrome)
high.action: full complement workup (C3NeF, sC5b-9, factor H/I/B levels, AH50); complement genetics panel (CFH, CFI, CFB, C3); nephrology referral; consider eculizumab for severe or refractory disease; pre-transplant complement assessment mandatory (50% recurrence in transplant)

moderate.label: 🟡  60–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: probable C3G; urgent nephrology referral for kidney biopsy; complete complement studies and autoimmune exclusion panel; note: positive ANA/ANCA reduce score and redirect diagnosis

low.label: 🟢  <60 Low confidence
low.action: C3G unlikely; investigate other GN causes; if autoimmune markers are positive, pursue SLE nephritis, ANCA vasculitis, or monoclonal GN workup; complete C3/C4 and exclusion panel before concluding
